realizes.rationale: Resolves once and supplies the same pair to owner record collection and the review composition.
The composition emits a standalone answer; a browser-dependent partial response is the rejected alternative.
The subject set covers selected records and exactly the family/member identities returned by this response, including continuation pages.
The existing subject answer attaches the projection from its held comparison without another candidate resolution.

29.note: The deleted prefer-both-sides rule remains retired. compose_review delegates revision selection over the comparison page items. Every retained revision in the selected population is a head, with no predecessor-edge traversal. Two unique nonempty-side heads form a pair; a known-empty side is an addition/removal only when the other side has exactly one head. Multiple heads on either nonempty side render explicit ambiguity; no selected revision on either side yields an unresolved non-pair. Retain the former successor-edge account as historical, not current. Anchor: `select_subject_revisions`; `revision_selection`

51.note: The complete read resolves the bound candidate once, collects owner records and composes over that resolution. Catalogue and subject routes use that same bound pair and the public source inventory; there is no stored composed answer or caller-chosen memory path. Current converted memory comes from the two derived Git-tree indexes; canonical dataset constants and review-matrix construction are retired. The input recheck precedes the later family/applicability and meaning projection reads, so this module does not promise a last-after-every-read recheck. compose_review attaches recorded meaning effects from the candidate index already held by its resolution. _meaning_subjects selects the addressed invariant/family plus returned family/member identities on both sides and deduplicates exact record/kind pairs. A roster continuation therefore carries its returned members’ own steps; a source/path selector invents no knowledge record. The before index is only an identity fallback for retired or after-absent UUIDs. History is read from the after tree exclusively, with no extra route, candidate resolution or wait for the leaf-wide worklist.
